key_insight: A machine-learning-assisted screening pipeline can shrink a 60,000+ compound CaCu$_5$-type search space to a small set of magnet candidates, with 159 showing favorable axial anisotropy in DFT.
engineering_relevance: This workflow provides a scalable route to identify promising permanent-magnet materials before expensive first-principles calculations, accelerating materials design.
method: Screened with pretrained materials models, Materials Project data, and a magnetization predictor
Applied four filters: metallicity, negative formation energy, E$_\mathrm{hull}$ $\leq$ 50 meV/atom, and magnetization $\geq$ 0.75 T
evidence_signal: The screening reduced the chemical space to 439 DFT candidates, and 159 were found to have positive axial magnetic anisotropy favoring [001].
watch_item: Results depend on the accuracy and transferability of the pretrained models and thresholds, so some promising compounds may be missed or misranked.
paper_title: Data driven screening of CaCu$_5$-type magnetic structures
